why_angle: None of the cited pages (GeekChamp, IKEA's STENKOL/LADDA page, RottenWifi, GoMyReview) mentions that Tenergy's TN480U kits come without a wall adapter. None says the charger needs 5 V 2 A, or that Tenergy's own 20 W brick has only a USB-C port and no cable. This page puts a matching 5 V 2 A adapter in each Tenergy cart, warns against the brick that doesn't fit, and compares each kit's wall-power situation.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Cost per cell, charger and adapter included: the 16-cell Tenergy cart is $47.99 + $19.99 = $67.98, and $67.98 ÷ 16 = about $4.25 a cell. The starter cart is $32.49 + $19.99 = $52.48, and $52.48 ÷ 8 = about $6.56 a cell.
  • Time to fill an AA on the TN480U: 2,800 mAh ÷ 500 mA = 5.6 h at least. The starter's 2,500 mAh cells take 2,500 ÷ 500 = 5 h, and a Premium Pro AAA takes 1,100 ÷ 250 = 4.4 h. Real charges run longer because NiMH charging loses some energy. Tenergy doesn't publish a charge time.
  • Power the TN480U needs: 5 V × 2 A = 10 W. An old 5 V 1 A phone cube supplies 5 V × 1 A = 5 W, half the rated input.
  • Charge left after a year in a drawer: Tenergy rates Premium Pro cells at 85% after 1 year in storage, so an AA keeps 2,800 × 0.85 = 2,380 mAh.
  • Rated wear: Tenergy rates Premium Pro cells for up to 1,200 recharges and the starter cells for up to 1,000. Panasonic's listing for the eneloop 8-pack says 2,100 cycles.

Most homes: 16 cells across both sizes and 8 bays, so a full load of AA and AAA charges at once. It needs the 18 W adapter in the same cart. {kit:kit-tenergy-16-cell-aa-aaa}

Smaller start: the same 8-bay charger with 4 AA and 4 AAA. It costs less up front, has spare bays to grow into, and has cells rated for 1,000 recharges. {kit:kit-tenergy-starter-4-aa-4-aaa}

AA only: the eneloop charger plugs straight into the wall, is sold as a 3-hour charger, and its 8-pack cells are listed at 2,100 cycles. It charges only 4 cells at a time, and this kit has no AAA. {kit:kit-eneloop-12-aa}

The Tenergy box has no wall plug: add a 5 V 2 A adapter

Tenergy's listings for both TN480U combos say the charger takes DC 5 V 2 A through its Micro-USB or USB-C port. The 8 AA + 8 AAA listing says "Micro-USB to AC power adapter is NOT included" and puts one Micro-USB cable in the box. The 4 AA + 4 AAA starter box lists only the charger and the cells.

Tenergy's 18 W kit (P/N 59088) covers both gaps. Its wall charger is rated 5 V 2 A, plus 9 V 2 A and 12 V 1.5 A, 18 W max. It comes with two 6 ft USB-to-Micro-USB cables and a car charger. That is why both Tenergy carts include it.

The TN480U charges NiMH and NiCd cells only. Keep 1.5 V lithium AA cells out of it. GeekChamp: "Do not put regulated lithium cells in a charger that supports only NiMH."

The other two chargers plug into the wall themselves. HKJ's BudgetLightForum test of the eneloop BQ-CC55 found a foldable US plug. It also found one 3 A charging circuit switched between 2 or 4 channels, so each cell gets less current with all four slots full, and a -dV/dt cut-off followed by a 1-hour top-off at around 140 mA. IKEA says STENKOL connects directly to a wall socket, takes NiMH cells of at least 1,000 mAh (AA) or 500 mAh (AAA), and fills them in 4–8 hours.

Not recommended

Don't buy a TN480U combo on its own, or pair it with Tenergy's USB-C PD 20W charger. Without an adapter, the charger has nothing to plug into a wall socket. The 20 W brick has a single USB-C port and comes with no cable. Tenergy doesn't say whether the TN480U accepts power over a USB-C-to-USB-C cable. The 18 W kit is the Tenergy adapter that matches the 5 V 2 A rating and includes the cable.
